title: Trump’s AI Liability Push Opens Blame Game for Models Gone Rogue
summary: The Trump administration’s embrace of legal liability to enforce artificial intelligence safety sets the stage for future conflicts over who foots the bill when AI models go rogue: the companies that design the systems or the people that deploy the technology.

title: The Race for AI Supremacy Raises Safety Concerns
summary: Technology Journalist and Author Kevin Roose tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a relatively small group of researchers and executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind has driven the race toward artificial general intelligence, raising questions about who controls the technology and its potential risks. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Roose discusses his new book, The AGI Chronicles, and the challenges of regulating increasingly capable AI systems as developers pursue technology that could surpass human intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Turkey Bans Social Media Accounts for Children Under 15
summary: Turkey has barred social media platforms from providing services to children under the age of 15, according to a regulation published in the Official Gazette.

title: Anthropic AI Model Went Rogue, Submitted Fake Tip to Police
summary: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations, including submitting a false tip in a police homicide case, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems.

title: Super Micro Case ‘Fixer’ Pleads Guilty to Diverting AI Tech
summary: A man charged along with Super Micro Computer Inc. co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw of conspiring to send cutting-edge chips to China in violation of US export controls pleaded guilty, according to court documents.

title: Cirrus Logic Is Said to Have Bid for Synaptics After Onsemi Deal
summary: Semiconductor company Cirrus Logic Inc. made an unsolicited acquisition offer for Synaptics Inc. last month as it looked to spoil a previously announced deal with On Semiconductor Corp., according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber on AI Agents & The Great Tech Divide
summary: Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the findings of the company's CTRL Tomorrow study on how tech impacts its users, finding opportunity in the AI era, and why design-led hardware still has a major role to play. Faber speaks with Bloomberg's Carol Massar and Jess Menton. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Andreessen Horowitz Backs Jev Maker at $7.5 Billion Value
summary: TypeSafe AI, the startup behind Jev, a new artificial intelligence model that went viral after it launched only a few weeks ago, has raised about $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation in a financing led by Andreessen Horowitz.

title: Ramp Hits $60 Billion Valuation in $1.85 Billion Funding Round
summary: Fintech startup Ramp has reached a roughly $60 billion valuation with its latest fundraising effort, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Surveillance Pricing May Be Coming to a Store Near You
summary:
What if the electronic shelf label you see at the grocery store isn't just showing you the price of the jar of mayonnaise you're about to buy — but actually raising the price because you put a can of tuna in your cart.

It's called surveillance pricing and retailers like Walmart appear to be locking down technology that will help them figure out how much they can charge you. Bloomberg's Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody's Business podcast to unpack this pricing strategy (which Walmart has denied using).  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lockheed Unveils New Patriot For US Army Air Defense Contest
summary: Lockheed Martin Corp. unveiled a new missile interceptor designed to outperform its most capable Patriot variant, as the US Army seeks to expand its air defense capabilities against increasingly sophisticated threats like hypersonic missiles.

title: OpenAI's $70B Run Rate Meets AI's Infrastructure Challenge
summary: loomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's latest annualized revenue, expected to reach or exceed $70 billion by the end of the year. Plus, Oracle keeps several data centers on track by relying on truck deliveries of natural gas, and a conversation with Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman on the mega AI IPO pipeline and the future of physical AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic and OpenAI Use Different Revenue Calculations, Clouding AI Valuations
summary: When measuring the race between artificial intelligence leaders OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, investors have run into a problem: The two private companies calculate a closely watched revenue figure differently.

title: Why Finance Execs Are Counting Every Token
summary: Workers running up their AI use, or 'tokenmaxxing,' has given way to value-maxing, but AI spend is still keeping chief financial officers up at night. Bloomberg's Nina Trentmann joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" for a deep dive into this week's CFO Briefing Newsletter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oracle Trucking Gas to Keep Data Centers on Track
summary: Oracle is using a new power strategy to keep many of its data centers on track: trucking natural gas directly to the server farms. The company is considering using this approach to speed up a build in New Mexico, where a gas pipeline needed to help power one of its crucial data centers is delayed. Bloomberg's Brody Ford joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" to discuss Oracle's strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: From Anthropic to Waymo: Kleiner Perkins Bets on AI’s Next Act
summary: Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman says AI is still in the early stages of reshaping the economy, with opportunities extending from frontier models like Anthropic to consumer agents, autonomous vehicles and robotics. He discusses why the firm sees physical AI as a potential source of the next trillion-dollar companies, the rapid growth of leading private AI businesses, and why he’s increasingly optimistic about both the IPO and M&A markets. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Visa Crackdown Raises Questions for Tech Talent
summary: The Trump administration has suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several other companies and universities from a program used to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency, citing concerns about potential abuse. Erickson Immigration Group attorney Hiba Anver explains why restrictions on employment-based immigration could have broader implications for the technology industry’s talent pipeline. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SoftBank-Backed OPay Wins $185 Million Standard Bank Placement
summary: SoftBank Group Corp.-backed OPay Digital Services Ltd. secured about $185 million in a private placement with Africa’s biggest bank as it prepares to list in the US.

title: Disney’s ‘Star Wars’ Strategy Is Working Out Much Better for Video Games
summary: Video games like ‘Star Wars Zero Company’ have been both critically and commercially successful

title: Bearish Bond Narrative Has Gone Too Far, Deutsche Bank Says
summary: The swing to deeply-negative sentiment on fixed-income assets this year has gone too far, with the market underpricing the risk of an artificial-intelligence blowup that triggers a rush into bonds, according to Deutsche Bank AG’s George Saravelos.
